there are so many everyday demos that could make ai, personal agents, & agents in general feel insanely powerful to normal ppl & yet ai companies keep choosing things like booking flights, planning travel, or god forbid planning a god damn wedding.

these are not everyday problems. they’re relatively rare events & worse for a lot of ppl they’re actually part of the joys of life. the best demo should make someone feel pain they already are familiar with disappearing. almost every company gets this wrong. they optimize for spectacle instead of relief which is fine in some cases but it doesn’t last.

one of my favorite historical examples is a product called head on.

the ad showed someone with a headache, then showed them applying the product directly to their forehead while repeating:

“head on. apply directly to the forehead.”

beautifully simple. you instantly understood the product, the problem, & the value. ai companies should be doing the same thing.

show me the annoying thing i deal with every single day then make it disappear. it’s not sexy, i guarantee it will work. when jobs demo’ed the iphone he picked universal simple problems that the iphone did better than anything else on the fucking planet.

anyway, thanks for coming to my ted talk.

candidates.text:
For anyone interested in the media math on Cody's bio auction:

I get ~3k profile views per month. Cody's audience is 12x bigger than mine = ~36k views per month, ~72k over 2 months. At the current $15k bid, that backs out to a ~$208 CPM.

The scaling assumption is conservative: his posts likely travel further, so profile views could be way higher, bringing the CPM down more.

But CPM isn't really the point. Even if only ~4k of those viewers are actual DTC decision-makers, that's ~$3.75 per buyer reached for 2 months vs $50/head at a conference.

And if your software costs more than $15k a year, you only need to close 1 customer to break even.

$15k feels defensible for any sponsor selling to DTC operators.

When the acquisition process falls through a few times, your resolve to sell the company drops significantly.

Founders can do their best, but life happens, and their months of work fail in a day. They bet their company's future on the transaction, and there's no alternate route.

And no one on the outside gets how energy draining and soul sucking this whole thing is.

Some founders want to make sure their customers are taken care of.
Some founders want to take care of the team.
Some founders want to have an exit story to tell.

Whatever your reason, kudos to founders who still keep working to sell the company, and eventually do.

It’s been my first true career break in six years and has been the most opportune moment to have free time 

Astra and fable 5.1 launched. Grok bot, instinct, muse, and dot followed. I set up my harnesses, been testing and vibe coding with all the agents. I got my website live, launched defi native skill, and the sponsor me index. Markets have been turning around. So many new onchain products have been launching and volumes returning. Outside of playing with AI, I’ve spent it with family in asia and finally got the chance to explore mainland china

It started with wanting to see robots in shenzhen. Then i went off to shanghai, chongqing, and sichuan province. They love pandas here! I’ve been navigating daily with the super apps, payment networks, and local models. Been intentionally experiencing and observing how technology is used in an environment that pushes to accelerate it. Also taking note on how fintechs are marketed in asia - oh, and riding in the latest evs lol 

I’m grateful for this time to explore. I learned a lot on capital markets and onchain trading infra in my last chapter and now reflecting on what’s durable for my next 5+ year bet. If there’s any interviews, substacks, books you loved listening and reading recently, please send it my way :)

This is actually really important. TLDR

Computer chips have always been limited by the tiny electrical wires that carry data to and from memory. Those wires only work over very short distances. 

These guys are working on replacing many of those wires with beams of light from miniature lasers. (Pew pew very sci-fi) 

Light can obviously travel farther inside the package, which would let one chip output far more (or rather be orders of magnitude more efficient than) than current systems. Incredibly valuable for 🇺🇸 right now.
